faq.charcount.0.q: Which count do Korean job applications use — with or without spaces?
faq.charcount.0.a: It depends on the company. If the form says “including spaces”, use that number; if it says nothing, including spaces is the usual assumption. Both numbers are shown, so check them together.
faq.charcount.1.q: Why are there two byte counts?
faq.charcount.1.a: In UTF-8 a Korean syllable takes 3 bytes; in EUC-KR it takes 2. Message boards, SMS and database limits are written against one encoding or the other, so both are shown.
faq.charcount.2.q: Does the text I type go anywhere?
faq.charcount.2.a: Nothing is sent to a server — the counting all happens in your browser. It is kept briefly in **this browser’s storage** so a refresh does not lose your work; “Clear” removes it, and it never reaches another device or a server.
faq.charcount.3.q: What is the manuscript-page count based on?
faq.charcount.3.a: The Korean 200-character manuscript sheet (20 boxes per line, 10 lines per sheet). A line break throws away the rest of that line, so the sheet count can be higher than characters ÷ 200 — that is how real sheets fill up.
faq.charcount.4.q: Why do I get a warning when I add an emoji?
faq.charcount.4.a: EUC-KR, the older Korean encoding, cannot hold characters like emoji. If the byte limit you are working against is EUC-KR, pasting them can break or get rejected, so you are told in advance.
faq.charcount.5.q: How is the reading time worked out?
faq.charcount.5.a: It assumes 500 characters a minute reading silently and 300 characters a minute reading aloud, for Korean text. Handy for sizing a script you have to present.
faq.qrgen.0.q: Does the QR code I make expire?
faq.qrgen.0.a: No. The content sits inside the QR itself rather than behind a shortened URL, so it keeps working for as long as the image exists.
faq.qrgen.1.q: Which error-correction level should I pick?
faq.qrgen.1.a: M is plenty for ordinary use. Choose H if you are putting a logo in the middle or printing onto something that may get damaged. The higher the level, the denser the QR.
faq.qrgen.2.q: How do I use the WiFi QR?
faq.qrgen.2.a: Enter the network name (SSID), the password and the security type. Pointing a camera at it connects without typing the password. It works with the stock iOS and Android cameras.
faq.qrgen.3.q: What is the minimum size for printing?
faq.qrgen.3.a: At least 2cm × 2cm in the real world, with a quiet margin of at least four module widths around it. The margin is added for you.
faq.qrgen.4.q: I added a logo and it says it cannot be read.
faq.qrgen.4.a: The logo is covering too many modules. Shrink it, or raise the error correction to H (30%). This tool actually re-reads the QR it made, so keep adjusting until the message turns green.
faq.jsonfmt.0.q: Is it safe to paste an API response in here?
faq.jsonfmt.0.a: Parsing happens only in your browser and nothing is sent to a server. On a shared computer, do clear the box when you are done.
faq.jsonfmt.1.a: Standard JSON does not allow comments, so it is reported as an error. If you use JSONC or JSON5, strip the comments first.
faq.jsonfmt.2.q: How large a JSON can it handle?
faq.jsonfmt.2.a: As large as the browser’s memory allows. A few megabytes is usually fine, but very large files make the display sluggish.
faq.jsonfmt.3.q: What gets copied when I click a line in the tree?
faq.jsonfmt.3.a: The path to that value — something like `$.users[0].name`, which you can paste straight into code, jq or a JSONPath expression.
faq.jsonfmt.4.a: It never changes anything by itself. For common slips — trailing commas, single quotes, comments, unquoted keys — it offers “fix it like this” only when the fixed version actually parses, and you decide whether to take it. Silently rewriting your input would hide what was wrong.
faq.base64.0.q: Why does non-Latin text come out broken?
faq.base64.0.a: The browser’s built-in function works on bytes, so passing text like Hangul straight in throws an error. Here it is encoded as UTF-8 going in and read back as UTF-8, so nothing breaks.
faq.base64.1.q: When do I need the URL-safe form?
faq.base64.1.a: The + and / in Base64 mean other things inside a URL. When the value travels in an address or a token, the - and _ form is used instead. JWTs work this way.
faq.base64.2.a: No. It is just a way of writing bytes down, and anyone can reverse it. If you need something kept secret, encrypt it.
faq.uuidgen.0.q: Should I use v4 or v7?
faq.uuidgen.0.a: v4 is enough for most things. v7 helps where sorting by creation order matters, such as a database primary key — its leading bits are the timestamp, so indexes fragment less.
faq.uuidgen.1.a: UUID v4 carries 122 random bits, so collisions are not a practical concern. Note that v7 exposes the creation time inside the value, so it is a poor fit when that has to stay hidden.
faq.uuidgen.2.q: Can I use the passwords this makes?
faq.uuidgen.2.a: They come from the browser’s cryptographic randomness and are never stored or transmitted. On a shared computer, clear the screen when you are done.
faq.hashgen.0.q: Does the file get uploaded to a server?
faq.hashgen.0.a: No. It is hashed locally with the browser’s WebCrypto, and no data leaves over the network.
faq.hashgen.1.q: Can I store passwords as MD5?
faq.hashgen.1.a: Please don’t. MD5 and SHA-1 have known collisions and should only be used to check integrity. For passwords use a purpose-built algorithm such as bcrypt or argon2.
faq.hashgen.2.q: Does it handle very large files?
faq.hashgen.2.a: The whole file is loaded into memory, so multi-gigabyte files can be too much for a browser. For those, an OS command (certutil, sha256sum) is the better tool.
faq.timer.0.q: Is it accurate while I am looking at another tab?
faq.timer.0.a: Yes. Instead of counting frames it takes the difference between the start time and now, so error does not pile up even when the browser slows a background tab down.
faq.timer.1.a: Browsers block sound until the page has been clicked at least once. If you started it with the Start button it will ring normally. Check that the device is not muted too.
faq.timer.2.q: Will it alert me if I close the window?
faq.timer.2.a: No — the tab has to stay open. If you need an alarm that wakes a sleeping computer, use the Alarm tool in the KarmoLab desktop app.
faq.datecalc.0.a: If the birthday has passed it is (this year − birth year); if not, one less. Since June 2023 this so-called “full age” is the single legal age in Korea.
faq.datecalc.1.q: Is the target day D-0 or D-1?
faq.datecalc.1.a: Here the target day itself is D-DAY and the day before is D-1. Places that follow a different convention can be one day off.
faq.datecalc.2.q: Are public holidays taken out of the business-day count?
faq.datecalc.2.a: Only Saturdays and Sundays are removed. Public holidays move from year to year and are not included, so subtract them yourself if you need to.
faq.unitconv.0.q: How many square metres is one Korean pyeong?
faq.unitconv.0.a: One pyeong is about 3.3058m². The other way round, 1m² is about 0.3025 pyeong.
faq.unitconv.1.q: Is data size based on 1000 or 1024?
faq.unitconv.1.a: The binary basis, where 1KB = 1024B. Storage manufacturers label their products on the 1000 basis, so the numbers can differ.
faq.unitconv.2.q: How many grams is one Korean geun?
faq.unitconv.2.a: It is worked out here as 600g. In practice meat uses 600g while vegetables and fruit use 375g, so it depends on the item.
faq.unitconv.3.q: How is the price per pyeong worked out?
faq.unitconv.3.a: The area above is converted to pyeong and the total is divided by it. For example 84m² (25.41 pyeong) at 600 million won is about 23.6 million won per pyeong, or about 7.14 million per m². Whether you entered the gross or the net floor area is for you to check.
faq.textdiff.0.q: Does it show characters that changed inside a line?
faq.textdiff.0.a: Comparison is by line at the moment. If a single character differs, that whole line shows as added and removed.
faq.textdiff.1.q: How long can the texts be?
faq.textdiff.1.a: Up to 2,000 lines each. Beyond that it compares the beginning and tells you it was cut. The limit is there because the diff algorithm can freeze a browser on very long input.
faq.textdiff.2.q: Can I use it for code?
faq.textdiff.2.a: Yes. It uses a monospace font and shows line numbers on both sides. There is no syntax highlighting though.
faq.textdiff.3.q: Can I see only the part that changed within a line?
faq.textdiff.3.a: Yes. When an added line follows a removed one, it is treated as “one line rewritten” and only the differing characters are shown in bold. Korean has few spaces, so splitting by word would make the whole line look changed — it works character by character.
faq.regextest.0.q: Which regex flavour does it use?
faq.regextest.0.a: The browser’s own JavaScript (ECMAScript) engine. Syntax specific to Python or PCRE will not work.
faq.regextest.1.a: g searches the whole string, i ignores case, m makes ^ and $ work per line, s lets . match newlines, and u turns on Unicode handling.
faq.regextest.2.q: Are there patterns that freeze the browser?
faq.regextest.2.a: Nested repetition such as (a+)+b can slow down sharply on certain input. Matching stops at 5,000 hits here, but patterns like that are dangerous in production too, so they are best avoided.
faq.colorconv.0.q: What does a contrast ratio of 4.5:1 mean?
faq.colorconv.0.a: It is the minimum contrast the WCAG accessibility guidelines ask for on body text. 4.5 or more meets AA, 7 or more meets AAA, and text at 18pt and above passes at 3:1.
faq.colorconv.1.q: The CMYK values differ from what my printer says.
faq.colorconv.1.a: Screens (RGB) and print (CMYK) cover different ranges, and an accurate conversion needs a colour profile. The values here are a profile-less approximation, so use professional tools for print proofing.
faq.colorconv.2.q: How is the harmony palette built?
faq.colorconv.2.a: By rotating the angle on the HSL colour wheel: 180° for the complement, 120° and 240° for the triad, and ±30° for the analogous colours.
faq.asciiart.0.q: Does the image get uploaded to a server?
faq.asciiart.0.a: No. It is read and processed on a browser canvas, and no data leaves over the network.
faq.asciiart.1.a: Monospace characters are taller than they are wide. That ratio is corrected automatically, but wide line spacing where you paste it can stretch it again. Keep the line height near 1.0.
faq.asciiart.2.a: Images with strong contrast and a simple background. For people, cropping tightly to the face reads much better.
faq.asciiart.3.a: “Add colour” is for the on-screen preview only. Copying the text or saving the PNG gives you a single colour.
faq.specialchar.0.q: It shows as a box (□) when I paste it.
faq.specialchar.0.a: The font does not carry that character. Use a different font, or pick a character with wider support.
faq.specialchar.1.q: Can I type special characters from a Korean keyboard?
faq.specialchar.1.a: Press a consonant such as ㅁ, ㅂ or ㅅ and then the Hanja key to get a list. That list is small though, so this table is faster.
faq.specialchar.2.q: What is the value starting with U+?
faq.specialchar.2.a: The Unicode code point. You use it for \u escapes in code or as an HTML numeric reference.
faq.ascii.0.q: What is the difference between ASCII and Unicode?
faq.ascii.0.a: ASCII is an early standard that defines only 128 characters; Unicode contains those same 128 and adds the writing systems of the world. In UTF-8 the ASCII range is still one byte.
faq.ascii.1.q: Is keyCode the same value as the ASCII code?
faq.ascii.1.a: No. The keyCode on a keyboard event is based on key position, so it can disagree with the character code. If you need the key itself, use the keyboard event code table.
faq.ascii.2.a: 128–255 is called extended ASCII, but there is no single standard for it — it differs by environment. Only the standard range is listed here to avoid the confusion.
faq.htmlentity.0.q: Can I not just write the character directly?
faq.htmlentity.0.a: In a UTF-8 document you usually can. But <, > and & clash with the markup itself, so those must be written as entities.
faq.htmlentity.1.a: Where a line must not break — between a number and its unit, for example. Using several in a row to push things apart is a job for CSS instead.
faq.htmlentity.2.q: What are the numeric ones like ₩?
faq.htmlentity.2.a: A way of naming a character by its Unicode number. You use it when the character has no named entity.
faq.httpstatus.0.q: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
faq.httpstatus.0.a: 401 means “I do not know who you are” — you need to sign in. 403 means “I know who you are, and you are not allowed”.
faq.httpstatus.1.a: Use 301 when the address has moved permanently; search engines carry the ranking over to the new one. For something temporary, use 302 or 307.
faq.httpstatus.2.q: What is the difference between 404 and 410?
faq.httpstatus.2.a: 404 means “not here right now”, 410 means “gone for good”. Returning 410 gets it dropped from the index faster.
faq.colorname.0.q: Is it fine to use colour names directly?
faq.colorname.0.a: Every browser supports them, so yes. Inside a design system, though, variables that carry meaning are easier to maintain.
faq.colorname.1.q: Do both gray and grey work?
faq.colorname.1.a: Both are valid. This table lists the gray spelling.
faq.colorname.2.q: Where do the exact HEX values come from?
faq.colorname.2.a: They are asked of the browser itself. Nothing was copied by hand, so there are no typos.
faq.keycode.0.q: Should I use key or code?
faq.keycode.0.a: Use key when the character typed is what matters, and code when the physical key position matters (WASD movement and the like). code stays the same across keyboard layouts.
faq.keycode.1.a: It is deprecated in the standard. Refer to it only when maintaining old code; use key and code for anything new.
faq.keycode.2.a: Keys like F5 and Ctrl+W are taken by the browser first. A web page cannot intercept those.
faq.radix.0.q: Is it accurate for very large numbers?
faq.radix.0.a: Yes. It calculates with BigInt, so the value stays exact no matter how many digits there are — none of the rounding error you get from ordinary floating point.
faq.radix.1.a: Put a minus sign in front. It is written as a sign plus a magnitude, not as two’s complement.
faq.radix.2.q: Why is the binary broken into groups of four?
faq.radix.2.a: Four binary digits map exactly onto one hexadecimal digit, so grouping them makes it easy to line the two up by eye.
faq.textclean.0.q: In what order are the steps applied?
faq.textclean.0.a: Fixed: tidy whitespace → drop blank lines → remove duplicates → sort → change case → prefix and suffix → number the lines. Toggling a checkbox lets you compare the result immediately.
faq.textclean.1.a: Yes — it uses the Korean collation rules. Mixed with Latin text, each is placed by its own language rules.
faq.textclean.2.q: Does the text get sent to a server?
faq.textclean.2.a: No. Everything happens inside your browser and what you type is never sent anywhere.
faq.emoji.0.q: Why does searching in English sometimes miss things?
faq.emoji.0.a: The official emoji names are English but often unhelpful — “face with tears of joy” is not what anyone types. Extra search words are attached to each entry so everyday wording finds them.
faq.emoji.1.q: The emoji shows as a box.
faq.emoji.1.a: The device or browser has no font for it. The copied value itself is fine, so it will show properly wherever the font exists.
faq.emoji.2.q: Why do they look different on different devices?
faq.emoji.2.a: Emoji are characters, not pictures — Apple, Google, Samsung and others each draw their own font. The same character can look quite different.
faq.markdown.0.a: GitHub Flavored Markdown, the dialect GitHub uses. Tables, checkboxes and strikethrough — none of which were in the original Markdown — were added there.
faq.markdown.1.q: I copied it and it did not work.
faq.markdown.1.a: Support for tables, checkboxes and collapsible sections varies from editor to editor. Each entry notes where it works.
faq.markdown.2.q: How do I write a literal asterisk?
faq.markdown.2.a: Put a backslash in front of it. There is an escaping entry under “common snags”.
faq.percent.0.q: Why a row of sentences instead of one calculator?
faq.percent.0.a: Percentage questions use a different formula depending on which way round you ask. A single set of boxes leaves you guessing what goes where, so each question is written out as its own line.
faq.percent.1.q: Why do the increase and decrease not match?
faq.percent.1.a: 100 raised by 20% is 120, but getting from 120 back to 100 takes about 16.7% off, not 20% — because the number you measure against has changed.
faq.percent.2.q: Where do I calculate a price after a discount?
faq.percent.2.a: Use the “take N% off” line. For adding something on, like tax, use the “add N%” line.
faq.palette.0.q: Does the image get uploaded to a server?
faq.palette.0.a: No. It is read and processed entirely inside your browser and never transmitted anywhere.
faq.palette.1.a: By median cut — repeatedly splitting the colour cloud in half along its widest axis. Unlike simply counting the most frequent colours, an accent colour surrounded by a large background still survives.
faq.palette.2.q: Can I paste a screenshot straight in?
faq.palette.2.a: Yes. Copy your screen, paste it over this tool, and the palette appears right away.
faq.urlparse.0.q: Why do things like %EC appear in a URL?
faq.urlparse.0.a: A URL may only carry Latin letters, digits and a few symbols, so anything else — non-Latin letters, spaces — is rewritten in a fixed way. That rewriting is what %EC looks like.
faq.urlparse.1.q: Is it safe to remove tracking parameters?
faq.urlparse.1.a: Yes. Values like utm_source and fbclid exist to record where you clicked from, and the link goes to the same page without them. Stripping them makes a shared link tidier.
faq.urlparse.2.q: Does it work on text that is not a URL?
faq.urlparse.2.a: Encoding and decoding do. Splitting into parameters only works on a complete address starting with http://.
faq.gitcmd.0.q: Why is it organised by situation rather than command name?
faq.gitcmd.0.a: In git the name and the job rarely match. reset, revert and restore cannot be told apart by name — but ask “what do I want to undo” and only one answer fits.
faq.gitcmd.1.q: What is the difference between reset and revert?
faq.gitcmd.1.a: reset makes the commit as if it never happened; revert adds a new commit that undoes it. On a branch you share with others, revert is safer because it leaves history alone.
faq.gitcmd.2.q: I lost a commit by mistake.
faq.gitcmd.2.a: `git reflog` lists the commits you have recently been on. Find the hash there and go back to it — that usually recovers it.
faq.filetype.0.q: Does renaming the extension change the file format?
faq.filetype.0.a: No. Only the label changes; the contents stay as they were. Renaming a jpg to png leaves it a jpg, and some programs will refuse to open it. Use a converter instead.
faq.filetype.1.q: Is it safe to open a file I do not recognise?
faq.filetype.1.a: Anything executable — exe, apk, sh, ps1 — should not be opened when you do not know where it came from. Documents and images are usually safe, though older formats can carry vulnerabilities.
faq.filetype.2.q: My CSV opens with broken characters in Excel.
faq.filetype.2.a: The file’s encoding and the one Excel assumes do not match. Open it through Excel’s data-import step and choose UTF-8 there.
faq.shortcut.0.q: Why is this not the full list?
faq.shortcut.0.a: People open a shortcut table to find something they did not know, not to confirm what they already do. A full dump is harder to read, so only the ones you would actually reach for are kept.
faq.shortcut.1.q: What do I press instead of Ctrl on a Mac?
faq.shortcut.1.a: Command, mostly. Terminals and developer tools sometimes keep Ctrl as it is, so each entry says which one it means.
faq.shortcut.2.q: Can I reopen a tab I closed by accident?
faq.shortcut.2.a: Ctrl (Cmd) + Shift + T. Press it repeatedly and the tabs come back in order, going further into the past.
faq.caseconv.0.q: Does it handle names like XMLHttpRequest?
faq.caseconv.0.a: Yes. When a new word starts after a run of capitals, it splits there — XML · Http · Request.
faq.caseconv.1.q: Which style should I use where?
faq.caseconv.1.a: Usually camelCase for JavaScript variables, PascalCase for classes and components, snake_case for Python and database columns, kebab-case for URLs and CSS classes, and SCREAMING_SNAKE for constants and environment variables.
faq.caseconv.2.q: What about names in scripts without letter case?
faq.caseconv.2.a: Parts separated by spaces, underscores or hyphens are still split — but writing systems without upper and lower case (Hangul, kana, Han) gain little from a case conversion.
faq.jwt.0.q: Is it safe to paste a JWT in here?
faq.jwt.0.a: This tool decodes it inside your browser and sends it nowhere. But a JWT is signed plain text, not encryption — if the token itself leaks, anyone can read it and use it as is. Never paste a live token into a random site.
faq.jwt.1.q: Why does it not verify the signature?
faq.jwt.1.a: Verifying needs the secret or public key. Making people paste a secret key into a web page is itself dangerous, so it was deliberately left out.
faq.jwt.2.q: What do exp, iat and sub mean?
faq.jwt.2.a: exp is the expiry time, iat the issue time, and sub the subject the token refers to (usually the user ID). The times are seconds since 1970, so a human-readable time is shown alongside.
faq.cron.0.q: Why show the next run times as well?
faq.cron.0.a: A description still has to be interpreted; a time is simply right or wrong. If the time you expected does not appear, the expression is wrong and you see it immediately.
faq.cron.1.q: What happens if I set both day-of-month and day-of-week?
faq.cron.1.a: In standard cron it runs when *either* matches (OR). Setting the 1st and Monday together means it runs on the 1st of every month and on every Monday.
faq.cron.2.a: This handles the standard five fields (minute hour day month weekday) only. Six-field notation with seconds is an extension that only some programs use.
faq.lotto.0.a: No. Each Korean 6/45 draw is independent, so no condition can change the probability. It only saves you the work of picking numbers.
faq.lotto.1.a: Six distinct numbers from the browser’s randomness. It redraws until your conditions are met, and tells you if it gave up and drew without them.
faq.lotto.2.q: Why is there an odd/even balance option?
faq.lotto.2.a: Winning combinations often land between 2:4 and 4:2 odd to even. There is no probabilistic advantage — it is there for when you want that shape.
faq.ladder.0.q: Is the outcome decided in advance?
faq.ladder.0.a: No. The ladder is drawn at random first and shown on screen, then the path is actually walked down it. You can follow the drawn ladder yourself and check the result.
faq.ladder.1.a: From two to ten. Fewer and there is no ladder to speak of; more and the paths become hard to follow on a narrow screen.
faq.ladder.2.q: What if I leave the outcomes empty?
faq.ladder.2.a: It builds a default board where only the first line wins and the rest do not.
faq.hangulkey.0.q: Does it support the three-set (sebeolsik) layout?
faq.hangulkey.0.a: Only the standard two-set (dubeolsik) layout for now. Sebeolsik arranges the jamo differently, so the results would not match.
faq.hangulkey.1.q: Why do some letters stay as loose jamo?
faq.hangulkey.1.a: Because the actual typing order is reproduced exactly. If that order could never have formed a syllable, it stays as loose jamo.
faq.hangulkey.2.q: What happens to digits and symbols?
faq.hangulkey.2.a: Their key positions are the same on both layouts, so they are left untouched.
faq.hangulkey.3.q: Does it handle text with Hangul and Latin mixed?
faq.hangulkey.3.a: Yes. In something like “안녕 gktpdy” the Hangul run is turned back into Latin and the Latin run into Hangul, each on its own. Judging the whole text one way would flip the half that was already fine and make it worse. Digits and symbols are left alone.
faq.worldclock.0.q: Why does memorising the offset go wrong?
faq.worldclock.0.a: Daylight saving. The US and Europe shift their clocks by an hour in spring and autumn, and the switch dates differ by country — so a fixed offset is an hour off for several months a year.
faq.worldclock.1.q: What are these times based on?
faq.worldclock.1.a: The time-zone database built into your browser, queried every time. Nothing is written into the code, so daylight-saving changes are picked up automatically.
faq.worldclock.2.q: Are there offsets of 30 or 45 minutes?
faq.worldclock.2.a: Yes. India is on a 30-minute offset and Nepal on 45. That is why offsets are shown as they are rather than rounded to whole hours.
faq.bmi.0.a: The WHO treats 30 and above as obese, while the Korean Society for the Study of Obesity holds that Asian populations carry more health risk at the same BMI and puts the line at 25. Health checks in Korea generally use the latter.
faq.bmi.1.q: Can BMI tell me whether I am healthy?
faq.bmi.1.a: Only loosely. It cannot tell muscle from fat, so people who train read higher than they are, and someone with little muscle can read “normal” while carrying a lot of body fat. Treat it as a rough indicator and confirm anything real with a doctor.
faq.bmi.2.a: Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. At 170cm that means dividing by 1.7 × 1.7 = 2.89.
faq.morse.0.q: Is there Morse code for Hangul?
faq.morse.0.a: Yes — a Korean Morse code laid down in 1926. It is keyed jamo by jamo rather than by syllable, and compound finals or vowels are sent as their basic parts.
faq.morse.1.q: How are spaces and letter breaks written?
faq.morse.1.a: One space between letters and a slash (/) between words. This tool reads and writes the same way.
faq.morse.2.q: Is the ratio of dot to dash fixed?
faq.morse.2.a: With the dot as 1: the dash is 3, the gap between letters is 3, and the gap between words is 7. The audio follows the same ratio.
faq.morse.3.q: Reading Hangul back sometimes gives something different.
faq.morse.3.a: Korean Morse sends only jamo and never marks syllable boundaries, so ambiguity is built in. ㅅㅅ followed by a vowel can be read as 어쓰 or 엇스. Real operators resolved it from context; this tool picks one reading and shows it.
faq.pick.0.a: The list is shuffled by walking from the end and swapping with a random earlier position. The convenient trick of shuffling with a sort function is biased position by position, so it is not used here.
faq.pick.1.q: What if the team sizes do not divide evenly?
faq.pick.1.a: After shuffling, people are dealt out one at a time in turn, so no two teams differ by more than one person.
faq.pick.2.q: How is this different from the ladder?
faq.pick.2.a: The ladder pairs people with outcomes; this picks from or splits the list itself. When the path has to be visible, use the ladder.
faq.charmap.0.q: Why are the tables gathered in one place?
faq.charmap.0.a: All four do the same job — finding a character that is not on the keyboard and copying it. Kept apart, you first have to work out which table it lives in. The individual addresses still work.
faq.charmap.1.q: The symbol I copied looks broken elsewhere.
faq.charmap.1.a: That device or program has no font for the character. The copied value itself is fine.
faq.charmap.2.q: When do I need HTML entities?
faq.charmap.2.a: When a web document has to display a character that markup would otherwise eat, such as an angle bracket or an ampersand.
faq.reference.0.a: They are all tables you open because you do not remember something — the same kind of thing. Six of them standing side by side in a list makes it harder to see what is actually there.
faq.reference.1.q: Do the individual addresses still work?
faq.reference.1.a: They do. Arriving from a search for HTTP status codes or git commands opens that table’s page.
faq.reference.2.q: What are the tables based on?
faq.reference.2.a: Each table’s page says. Markdown follows the GitHub dialect; the shortcuts cover Windows, macOS, browsers and editors.
faq.interest.0.q: Why is the interest on a savings plan less than advertised?
faq.interest.0.a: Even at 4% a year, the money you pay in on the last month only works for a month. Only the first payment earns a full twelve months, so the real interest is a little over half of 4% of everything you paid in.
faq.interest.1.q: What is the 15.4% interest income tax?
faq.interest.1.a: Korea’s 14% income tax on interest plus 1.4% local income tax. It applies to the interest only, not the principal, and the bank withholds it before paying out.
faq.interest.2.q: Can the numbers differ from what my bank says?
faq.interest.2.a: Yes. It assumes simple interest and does not include bonus rates, tax-free products or compounding. Loans cover equal-instalment repayment only, with fees left out. Treat it as a rough estimate.
faq.pace.0.q: How do pace and speed differ?
faq.pace.0.a: Pace is how many minutes it takes you to run a kilometre; speed is how many kilometres you cover in an hour. They are reciprocals, so either one fixes the other.
faq.pace.1.q: Why does working it out by hand go wrong?
faq.pace.1.a: Pace is minutes and seconds — base 60 — while speed is decimal. Treating 6 minutes 30 as 6.3 throws the result off.
faq.pace.2.q: Are the half and full marathon distances exact?
faq.pace.2.a: They use the official distances: 21.0975km for the half and 42.195km for the full.
faq.workdays.0.a: That does not match reality. A deadline like “within 7 business days” only lands on the right date once public holidays and substitute holidays are taken out too. Korean Lunar New Year or Chuseok pushes it back by days.
faq.workdays.1.q: Why does it list the days it removed?
faq.workdays.1.a: Handing back a date alone leaves you no way to check it. Every removed day is listed with its reason, so if your company’s rules differ you see it at once.
faq.workdays.2.a: Korean Lunar New Year, Chuseok and Buddha’s Birthday follow the lunar calendar, so their solar dates change every year and cannot be derived by calculation. For a year that is not in the table it says so — it never quietly hands back a wrong date.
faq.workdays.3.a: Turn on “Saturdays count as business days” and they are included.
faq.workdays.4.q: Does the start day count as one?
faq.workdays.4.a: By default counting begins the next day. Some rules include the start day, so it is offered as an option.
faq.color.0.q: Why are the three tools in one place?
faq.color.0.a: All three exist to settle on one colour. Kept apart, you first have to decide which one to open. Each tool keeps its own address.
faq.color.1.q: Does the image get uploaded to a server?
faq.color.1.a: No. Colour extraction happens inside your browser and the image is never sent anywhere.
faq.color.2.a: Text is hard to read when it is too close in brightness to its background. The convert tab shows that number alongside, so you can judge readability while choosing the colour.
faq.text.0.q: Does what I type go to a server?
faq.text.0.a: No. Everything happens inside your browser and nothing is sent anywhere.
faq.text.1.q: Why put them all in one widget?
faq.text.1.a: Pasting, counting, tidying and comparing tend to happen one after another. With separate tools you would have to leave the screen and come back each time.
faq.text.2.a: They are still there. Arriving from a search for character counting or the like opens that tool’s page.
faq.calc.0.q: Why gather them in one place?
faq.calc.0.a: Calculators scattered one by one make it hard to see what exists. Tabs put them where you can pick at a glance.
faq.calc.1.a: They are still there. A search for a percentage calculator or unit conversion opens that tool.
faq.calc.2.q: Can the results differ from reality?
faq.calc.2.a: Interest and BMI each state their basis and their limits under the tab. Treat them as a reference.
faq.time.0.q: Is daylight saving taken into account?
faq.time.0.a: Yes. The time-zone data is queried each time, so the seasonal switch applies automatically.
faq.time.1.q: Does the timer keep running when I switch tabs?
faq.time.1.a: These are tabs within the same screen, so it keeps going. Closing the browser resets it.
faq.time.2.q: Where do I calculate an age?
faq.time.2.a: Age is inside the date tab.
faq.draw.0.q: Is the outcome decided in advance?
faq.draw.0.a: No. The ladder is drawn first and then walked; the draw shuffles the list at random.
faq.draw.1.q: What is the difference between the three?
faq.draw.1.a: Use the ladder to pair people with outcomes, the draw to pick from or split a list, and lotto when you need numbers.
faq.draw.2.q: Can the same person be picked twice?
faq.draw.2.a: No. Selections are made without repeats.
faq.devtool.0.q: Do the values I type go to a server?
faq.devtool.0.a: No. Everything is handled inside your browser and nothing is sent anywhere.
faq.devtool.1.q: Why gather them in one place?
faq.devtool.1.a: These get used for a moment at a time while developing. Scattered one by one, you would have to hunt through the list every time.
faq.devtool.2.a: They are. A search for a JSON formatter or a regex tester opens that tool.
faq.epoch.0.q: How does it know whether it is seconds or milliseconds?
faq.epoch.0.a: By the number of digits: 10 is seconds, 13 is milliseconds. Getting it wrong lands you near 1970 or far in the future, so the reading it used is shown on screen.
faq.epoch.1.a: The time elapsed since midnight UTC on 1 January 1970, written as a single number. It is the same value regardless of time zone, which is why logs and APIs use it.
faq.epoch.2.a: Your device’s zone and UTC, side by side. The ISO 8601 form is shown too.
faq.lorem.0.q: Why does the dummy text need to be in my own language?
faq.lorem.0.a: Character width, line breaking and letter spacing differ completely between scripts. Latin lorem ipsum cannot verify a layout that will actually hold Korean, Japanese or Chinese text.
faq.lorem.1.a: A fragment of Latin long used in the printing trade. Because it cannot be read for meaning, it became the standard filler for keeping attention on the design.
faq.lorem.2.q: Does the generated text mean anything?
faq.lorem.2.a: No. Words are strung together at random precisely so that it does not read.
faq.csvjson.0.q: Why do values containing commas survive?
faq.csvjson.0.a: CSV wraps a value in quotes when it contains a comma or a line break. Splitting naively on commas shifts the columns, so this reads character by character and tracks whether it is inside quotes.
faq.csvjson.1.q: My CSV looks broken when opened in Excel.
faq.csvjson.1.a: That is a character-encoding problem. Open it through Excel’s data-import step and choose UTF-8.
faq.csvjson.2.q: What does automatic number detection do?
faq.csvjson.2.a: It puts a value like 30 in as a number rather than a string. Turn it off to keep everything exactly as written.
faq.regexref.0.q: Why is it organised by what you are trying to do?
faq.regexref.0.a: In a regular expression a single symbol is the rule, so you get stuck at “what was that symbol again”. Searching by intent is faster than scanning a list of symbols.
faq.regexref.1.q: Why does \w not match my language?
faq.regexref.1.a: \w means Latin letters, digits and the underscore only. To catch other scripts use a range such as [가-힣] or turn on the Unicode flag.
faq.regexref.2.a: A perfect email regex is effectively impossible. The one here is good enough for practical use; the real check is sending a confirmation mail.
faq.numword.0.q: Why is it so easy to get the digits wrong?
faq.numword.0.a: Numbers are written with a comma every three digits, but Korean and Japanese group them every four (man / eok / jo). The place you count and the place you read do not line up, which is where the slips come from.
faq.numword.1.a: Normally 10 is read as “ten” and 100 as “hundred”, but financial documents often write them as “one ten” and “one hundred”. Turn it on when you need that form.
faq.numword.2.q: How large a number does it handle?
faq.numword.2.a: Up to gyeong (10^16). Anything larger and it tells you so.
faq.aspect.0.q: Why does working it out by hand drift?
faq.aspect.0.a: Multiplying by a ratio gives a fraction, but pixels are whole numbers, so there is rounding. Resize a few times and that error piles up until the image is subtly squashed.
faq.aspect.1.a: Putting footage of a different ratio into a video edit leaves black bars top and bottom or left and right. Knowing the thickness in advance makes it easy to place subtitles and logos.
faq.aspect.2.a: Roughly 1.618 to 1. It is held to look visually stable and gets cited often in design.
faq.birth.0.a: If this year’s birthday has passed, subtract the birth year from this year; if not, subtract one more. Since June 2023 this so-called “full age” is the single legal age in Korea.
faq.birth.1.q: What is the zodiac animal based on?
faq.birth.1.a: The commonly used 1 January boundary. Some hold that it should follow the lunar new year, so people born early in the year may see it differently.
faq.birth.2.q: Why are the star-sign boundaries confusing?
faq.birth.2.a: Each sign starts on a different day of the month, so the split falls around the 22nd. The start dates are kept in a table here and read from it.
faq.birth.3.q: What is the difference between full age, year age and Korean age?
faq.birth.3.a: Full age subtracts the birth year once the birthday has passed — the default in Korean law and contracts since June 2023. Year age ignores the birthday and is simply this year minus the birth year; military service and youth protection law use it. Korean age is the old counting method: year age plus one.
faq.contrast.0.q: What does a contrast ratio of 4.5:1 mean?
faq.contrast.0.a: It expresses the difference in brightness between text and its background. Web accessibility guidelines set 4.5:1 as the floor for body text and 3:1 for large text.
faq.contrast.1.q: It looks fine to me but it says fail.
faq.contrast.1.a: How it feels changes a lot with screen brightness and the light around you. Outdoors in daylight, or on a cheap display, it often disappears — which is why there is a numeric bar at all.
faq.contrast.2.a: 18pt and above, or bold at 14pt and above. On screen that is roughly 24px, or bold 18.66px.
faq.timecalc.0.q: Why does a normal calculator get it wrong?
faq.timecalc.0.a: Typing 7 hours 45 as 7.45 makes it a decimal. 45 minutes is 0.75 of an hour, so the answer drifts. Here the 7:45 form is read as it is.
faq.timecalc.1.a: 1:25, 85m and 1.5h all work. The totals box takes the same formats.
faq.timecalc.2.a: It shows that the result rolled into the next day — useful for night shifts and anything else that crosses a date.
faq.replace.0.q: How is this different from find-and-replace in an editor?
faq.replace.0.a: Most editors show you nothing until you press the button. Here the hits are marked first, so you can check before running an edit that is hard to undo.
faq.replace.1.a: Searching for cat skips the cat inside concat. Only matches that sit on word boundaries count.
faq.replace.2.q: How do I use a regular expression?
faq.replace.2.a: Turn on the regex option and the pattern is read as written. In the replacement you can pull out a captured group with $1.
faq.grade.0.q: How is this different from a plain average?
faq.grade.0.a: An A in a 3-credit course does not weigh the same as an A in a 1-credit one. Adding the grades and dividing loses that difference, and the number stops matching your transcript.
faq.grade.1.a: It varies by school. Korean universities mostly use a 4.5 maximum and some use 4.3. Check the maximum printed on your transcript.
faq.grade.2.q: How does the target GPA work?
faq.grade.2.a: It combines the credits you have with the credits still to come and works backwards to the average you need across what is left. If even perfect scores cannot get there, it says so.
faq.vat.0.q: Can I not just take 10% off the gross?
faq.vat.0.a: No. The VAT inside 110,000 won is 10,000 — but 10% of 110,000 is 11,000. To pull VAT out of a gross amount you divide by 1.1.
faq.vat.1.a: Yes. It defaults to Korea’s 10%; type another rate if you need one.
faq.vat.2.a: They are rounded for display. How a real tax invoice handles them depends on the trade convention and the system issuing it.
faq.bytesize.0.q: Why does a 1TB drive show as 931GB?
faq.bytesize.0.a: The manufacturer writes 1TB meaning a trillion bytes, while the operating system counts in steps of 1024 — so the same capacity reads as about 931GiB. No space went missing; the counting differs.
faq.bytesize.1.a: A notation created to make the 1024 basis explicit. KB means 1000, KiB means 1024.
faq.bytesize.2.a: Both are in use. Storage and network speeds conventionally use 1000; memory and operating-system displays use 1024.
faq.slug.0.q: Can I not just put non-Latin letters in the URL?
faq.slug.0.a: It works. But sharing it turns the address into a long string of percent signs, which messengers cut off and nobody enjoys looking at.
faq.slug.1.a: It follows the Revised Romanization of Korean, syllable by syllable. Rules where neighbouring letters affect each other, such as consonant assimilation, are not applied, so it can differ from the official spelling.
faq.slug.2.a: The hyphen is the norm in URLs, and search engines read it as a word separator.
faq.listdiff.0.q: How is this different from comparing texts?
faq.listdiff.0.a: A text diff keeps the line order and shows where things changed. A list comparison ignores order and only asks what overlaps. For checking one roster against another, this is the right one.
faq.listdiff.1.a: A value that appears several times counts once.
faq.listdiff.2.q: Are entries that differ only in case treated as different?
faq.listdiff.2.a: By default they are treated as the same. Turn on the option if you need them distinguished.
faq.bizno.0.q: Can it tell me whether the number is really registered?
faq.bizno.0.a: No. It only checks that the last digit matches what the earlier digits compute to. Whether a Korean business registration number actually exists has to be looked up with the National Tax Service.
faq.bizno.1.q: Then what is it good for?
faq.bizno.1.a: It catches typos. One wrong digit breaks the calculation, so you can spot it before sending a lookup.
faq.bizno.2.q: What do the two middle digits mean?
faq.bizno.2.a: The type of business. 01–79 is an individual taxable business, 81–88 the head office of a for-profit corporation, 90–99 an individual tax-exempt business, and so on.
faq.jamo.0.a: Building initial-consonant search — the feature where typing ㄱㅁㅅ finds 고맙습니다 in a Korean app.
faq.jamo.1.q: File names from a Mac show as loose jamo.
faq.jamo.1.a: The same Hangul can be stored either as composed syllables or as separate jamo, and that is where this comes from. The put-back button joins them into syllables again.
faq.jamo.2.a: Yes. Compound finals such as those in 앉 and 값 are shown and put back as they are.
faq.wordfreq.0.a: It cuts common Korean particles off the end of a word. It is not a morphological analyser, so it is not perfect, but it largely stops 도구를 · 도구가 · 도구는 being counted as three different words.
faq.wordfreq.1.a: The number of distinct words divided by the total number of words. The lower it is, the more the same words are being repeated.
faq.wordfreq.2.q: Does the text go to a server?
faq.wordfreq.2.a: No. The counting happens inside your browser only.
faq.json2ts.0.q: Why not just look at the first element of an array?
faq.json2ts.0.a: That is risky — a field present only on some elements would disappear entirely. Here every element is merged, and anything present on only some of them is marked optional with a question mark.
faq.json2ts.1.a: If another element has a value, that type is used. If every element is null, it stays the null type.
faq.json2ts.2.q: Does the JSON go to a server?
faq.json2ts.2.a: No. It is processed inside your browser only.
faq.colorblind.0.q: Why should meaning never rest on colour alone?
faq.colorblind.0.a: Red–green colour vision deficiency, where the two look alike, affects about 8% of men. Splitting success and failure by colour alone erases the information for them.
faq.colorblind.1.q: How is “hard to tell apart” decided?
faq.colorblind.1.a: The two colours are converted for each type and the distance between them measured; below a threshold it counts as hard. This is a design check, not a medical diagnosis.
faq.colorblind.2.q: So what should I do instead?
faq.colorblind.2.a: Pair colour with shape, an icon or a label. Widening the difference in lightness helps too.
faq.loan.0.q: Why is the early payment almost all interest?
faq.loan.0.a: Interest is charged on the balance still owed. At the start the principal is untouched, so the interest is large; as you pay it down, the interest share shrinks.
faq.loan.1.a: Equal-principal costs the least interest in total but the early payments are heavy. Equal-instalment keeps the same amount every month, which makes planning easy. Interest-only-until-maturity has the lightest monthly burden and the largest total interest.
faq.loan.2.q: Can it differ from a real loan?
faq.loan.2.a: Yes. Early-repayment fees, stamp duty and variable rates are not included. Treat it as a way to gauge the scale.
faq.loan.3.q: How much do I gain by paying a little extra each month?
faq.loan.3.a: Enter an amount and it appears immediately. On 100 million won at 4.5% over 30 years, equal-instalment, paying 500,000 won extra a month finishes 211 months sooner and saves about 53.8 million won of interest. Early-repayment fees vary by loan and are left out.
faq.loan.4.q: What does a grace period change?
faq.loan.4.a: During the grace period the principal does not fall and you pay interest only, so the total interest rises — on 100 million won at 4.5%, a 12-month grace period adds 4.5 million won of interest.
faq.cssunit.0.q: What is the difference between rem and em?
faq.cssunit.0.a: rem is relative to the document root’s font size, em to the parent element’s. The same 1.5 becomes a different size depending on where it sits.
faq.cssunit.1.a: Because 16px is the default font size in most browsers. If you changed the root size, divide by that instead.
faq.cssunit.2.a: It is a print unit. On the web 1pt converts to about 1.333px.
faq.linebreak.0.q: Will my paragraphs all run together?
faq.linebreak.0.a: Blocks separated by a blank line are treated as paragraphs and left alone. Only the line breaks inside a paragraph are joined with a space.
faq.linebreak.1.q: English words are split with a hyphen.
faq.linebreak.1.a: When a line ends in a hyphen it is joined back up. That shape is common in text copied from a PDF.
faq.linebreak.2.q: Spaces appear inside my text where there were none.
faq.linebreak.2.a: In scripts written without spaces — Korean run together, Japanese, Chinese — word boundaries cannot be known, so a space is added to be safe. Tidy it up with find-and-replace if you need to.
faq.checklist.0.a: Nowhere. The list lives in the URL itself, so anyone with the link sees the same list — and losing the link loses the list.
faq.checklist.1.q: Is the checked state shared too?
faq.checklist.1.a: The state at the moment you made the link is carried with it. If the other person ticks something, your screen does not change — this is not live sharing.
faq.checklist.2.q: Can I have a lot of items?
faq.checklist.2.a: URLs have a length limit, so past a few dozen the link gets very long. It suits short lists.
faq.pdftool.0.q: Does the file get uploaded to a server?
faq.pdftool.0.a: No. Everything is handled inside your browser, so contracts, CVs and anything else you must not upload stay safe.
faq.pdftool.1.q: How do I write a page range?
faq.pdftool.1.a: Like 1-3,5,8-. Leaving a side empty means from the start or to the end. Leaving the whole box empty covers every page.
faq.pdftool.2.a: A file with an open password cannot be opened. Files with only editing restrictions sometimes go through.
faq.audiocut.0.q: Which formats can I save as?
faq.audiocut.0.a: MP3 or WAV. MP3 is far smaller for sending or uploading; WAV is lossless and better if you will edit it again. The MP3 encoder is only downloaded when you choose MP3, so it stays light otherwise.
faq.audiocut.1.q: Why is the fade on by default?
faq.audiocut.1.a: A waveform that stops dead makes a click. Laying the first and last 0.05 seconds down gently removes it.
faq.audiocut.2.q: Which formats can I put in?
faq.audiocut.2.a: Anything your browser can decode. MP3, WAV, M4A and OGG generally open.
faq.filetool.0.a: The files this work touches are usually contracts, CVs or recordings — the kind you would rather not leave on someone else’s server. The browser can do the job itself, so there is no reason to send them.
faq.filetool.1.q: There is a pause when I open a tab.
faq.filetool.1.a: The PDF engine is large and is fetched the first time you open that tab. After that it opens immediately.
faq.filetool.2.a: It depends on the device’s memory. Files of several hundred megabytes can be slow or fail.
faq.pdf2img.0.q: How is this different from a screenshot?
faq.pdf2img.0.a: A screenshot is tied to your screen resolution. A PDF holds vectors, so it can be redrawn at whatever scale you like — at 2× the text comes out crisp.
faq.pdf2img.1.q: Should I pick PNG or JPG?
faq.pdf2img.1.a: PNG is sharper when there is a lot of text. For photo-heavy pages where size matters, use JPG.
faq.pdf2img.2.q: Does the file go to a server?
faq.pdf2img.2.a: No. It is rendered inside your browser only.
faq.img2pdf.0.a: No. Each keeps its ratio, is scaled to the largest size that fits inside the margin, and is centred. Nothing is stretched to fill.
faq.img2pdf.1.q: Can I use it for documents I have to submit?
faq.img2pdf.1.a: The format is an ordinary PDF, so that is fine. Do check the resolution or size limits of whoever you are submitting to.
faq.img2pdf.2.q: How do I change the order?
faq.img2pdf.2.a: Clear it and add them again in the order you want. They are bundled exactly as added.
faq.ziptool.0.q: Why show the list before extracting?
faq.ziptool.0.a: With an archive someone sent you, often all you needed was to see what is inside. You can take just the file you want instead of unpacking everything.
faq.ziptool.1.a: They cannot be opened. Only ordinary ZIPs without a password are handled.
faq.ziptool.2.q: What does the compression level change?
faq.ziptool.2.a: Higher means smaller but slower. Photos and video are already compressed, so raising it barely shrinks them.
faq.pdfwatermark.0.a: Stamping the purpose onto a copy of an ID or a contract before sending it helps stop the file being reused elsewhere.
faq.pdfwatermark.1.q: Does it work with non-Latin text?
faq.pdfwatermark.1.a: Yes. The built-in PDF fonts have no Hangul, kana or Han characters, so passing them straight in fails — the text is drawn as an image and laid on instead.
faq.pdfwatermark.2.a: It is laid on as an image, so it is hard to remove by ordinary means. It is not, however, real protection.
faq.audiojoin.0.q: Why do differing sample rates matter?
faq.audiojoin.0.a: Joining 44.1kHz and 48kHz as they are makes the later part play fast or slow. Here everything is resampled to the highest rate first and then joined.
faq.audiojoin.1.q: There is a click at the seam.
faq.audiojoin.1.a: That comes from the waveform stopping abruptly. Turning on the seam fade lays it down for a fraction of a second and the click goes.
faq.audiojoin.2.q: Which formats can I save as?
faq.audiojoin.2.a: MP3 or WAV. Choose MP3 for sending and WAV if you will edit it again.
faq.imgbatch.0.q: Can the result end up larger than the original?
faq.imgbatch.0.a: Yes. Converting a small, simple PNG to JPG makes it bigger. That is why the size before and after is shown together.
faq.imgbatch.1.a: It is the smallest at the same quality. Every current browser supports it, though very old software may not open it.
faq.imgbatch.2.q: Do the photos go to a server?
faq.imgbatch.2.a: No. They are processed inside your browser only.
faq.filehash.0.a: Downloads get corrupted, and files sometimes come from somewhere other than the publisher. A matching value means not one character of the contents differs.
faq.filehash.1.a: A SHA-256 is 64 characters long. Comparing by eye makes it easy to miss a single different character in the middle.
faq.filehash.2.q: Does the file go to a server?
faq.filehash.2.a: No. It is read and hashed inside your browser only.
faq.crypto.0.q: Can I recover it if I forget the password?
faq.crypto.0.a: No. The key is derived from the password, so without the same password there is no way to get the original text back.
faq.crypto.1.q: The same text gives a different result every time.
faq.crypto.1.a: That is correct. A fresh random value is mixed in on every encryption. It travels inside the result, so decrypting is unaffected.
faq.crypto.2.q: Does what I type go to a server?
faq.crypto.2.a: It does not. Encryption and decryption both finish inside your browser, and neither the text nor the password is transmitted.
faq.crypto.3.a: No. It is a way of writing bytes down that anyone can reverse. If the content must stay hidden, use AES.
faq.moon.0.q: How is the moon phase calculated?
faq.moon.0.a: The moon waxes and wanes on a cycle of about 29.5 days. Counting the days since a reference point places today somewhere in that cycle, which gives the phase.
faq.moon.1.a: Step the date forward and find the day where the phase name turns to full moon.
faq.moon.2.q: Can it differ slightly from the real sky?
faq.moon.2.a: It uses an average cycle, so it can be about a day out. It is for gauging tonight’s shape, not for precise observation.
faq.imageedit.0.q: Does the image get uploaded to a server?
faq.imageedit.0.a: It does not. Everything is handled inside your browser, so the file never leaves your device.
faq.imageedit.1.q: Which formats can I save as?
faq.imageedit.1.a: PNG, JPEG or WebP. JPEG and WebP are lighter for photographs; use PNG when you need a transparent background.
faq.imageedit.2.q: Can I crop to a fixed ratio?
faq.imageedit.2.a: Yes. Pick a common ratio such as 1:1, 4:3 or 16:9, or crop freely.
faq.imageedit.3.a: As far as the device’s memory allows. For very large photos it is quicker to reduce the size first and then adjust.
faq.memo.0.a: Inside the browser you are using. Nothing is sent to a server, so they do not appear on your other devices.
faq.memo.1.q: What happens if I clear my browser data?
faq.memo.1.a: They go with it. Copy anything that has to last somewhere else.
faq.memo.2.q: Does it work in a private window?
faq.memo.2.a: It works while the window is open, but everything disappears when you close it.
faq.memo.3.a: None is imposed here. There is, however, a limit on how much the browser can store in total.
faq.video2gif.0.q: Where does the video get uploaded?
faq.video2gif.0.a: Nowhere. Reading the video and assembling the GIF both finish inside your browser. No network request happens at all, so private footage is safe here.
faq.video2gif.1.q: What do I change to make the file smaller?
faq.video2gif.1.a: Width has the biggest effect, then frames per second, then the number of colours. Footage where almost nothing moves is already much smaller, because unchanged areas are skipped automatically.
faq.video2gif.2.a: A GIF can hold at most 256 colours. Raise the colour count, or turn on dithering — it scatters the remaining error into neighbouring pixels so the banding is less visible.
faq.video2gif.3.q: Why does it take a while to build?
faq.video2gif.3.a: Every frame has to be pulled out of the video, then reduced in colour and compressed. The work grows with frames per second times the length of the section. Pick a short section and it finishes quickly.
faq.video2gif.4.q: Which videos can I put in?
faq.video2gif.4.a: Anything your browser can play. mp4, webm and mov generally open.
faq.video2audio.0.q: Where does the video get uploaded?
faq.video2audio.0.a: Nowhere. The browser decodes the audio out of the file itself, so no network request happens.
faq.video2audio.1.q: Which formats can I save as?
faq.video2audio.1.a: MP3 or WAV. For keeping or passing on a lecture or meeting recording, MP3 is far smaller. If you will edit it, choose lossless WAV.
faq.video2audio.2.a: If the audio codec is one the browser does not know, it cannot decode it. mp4, webm and mov generally work. When it fails, it tells you rather than doing nothing.
faq.videotool.0.q: Why are they gathered in one place?
faq.videotool.0.a: Once you have loaded a video, one thing tends to lead to another. Scattered across separate tools, you would have to find the file and load it again each time.
faq.videotool.1.a: Each engine is fetched only when you first open that tab. Features you never use do not slow anything down.
faq.videotrim.0.q: Why does trimming take as long as the section itself?
faq.videotrim.0.a: A browser has no way to re-assemble a video. Instead it actually plays the chosen section and captures the picture and sound as they go — so trimming 10 seconds takes about 10 seconds. This is not a workaround but the only route available in a browser, which is why the remaining time is shown plainly.
faq.videotrim.1.a: It is captured again, so it is not bit-for-bit identical to the original. In exchange, the file is never uploaded anywhere. If you need the original quality intact, an editing program is the better tool.
faq.videotrim.2.q: Why is it saved as webm?
faq.videotrim.2.a: It picks the most widely supported of the formats a browser can capture. webm opens in current browsers and in most editing tools.
faq.videotrim.3.q: I want to drop the sound.
faq.videotrim.3.a: Turn off “keep the sound” and only the picture is captured.
faq.screenrec.0.q: Where does the recording get uploaded?
faq.screenrec.0.a: Nowhere. Recording happens inside the browser, and the file goes nowhere until you download it yourself. That matters especially here, since the file contains your own screen.
faq.screenrec.1.q: The sound is not being captured.
faq.screenrec.1.a: System sound can only be captured when the browser is sharing a “tab” or the “entire screen”, and you have to enable audio sharing in the share dialog. Choosing a single window often captures no sound. The microphone is a separate switch.
faq.screenrec.2.q: I hit the browser’s stop-sharing instead of the stop button.
faq.screenrec.2.a: That finishes it the same way. Whatever had been captured up to then becomes the result.
faq.screenrec.3.a: It picks the most widely supported of the formats a browser can capture. webm opens in current browsers and in most editing tools.
faq.voicerec.0.a: The most common accident in recording is finding out afterwards that nothing was captured. The bars let you see the sound arriving. If it is nearly silent when you finish, it says so.
faq.voicerec.1.q: Which formats can I save as?
faq.voicerec.1.a: MP3 or WAV. MP3 is the default and travels well by message or email. If you will carry on editing with the audio cutter or joiner, choose lossless WAV.
faq.voicerec.2.q: It says the microphone is unavailable.
faq.voicerec.2.a: Click the lock in the address bar and allow microphone access. Another program holding the microphone can also block it.
faq.voicerec.3.a: When the input is too loud the bars turn red and the sound breaks up. Try speaking a little further from the microphone.
faq.pdfcompress.0.q: Where does the document get uploaded?
faq.pdfcompress.0.a: Nowhere. Opening it and rebuilding it both finish inside your browser — which suits contracts and copies of ID especially well.
faq.pdfcompress.1.q: I cannot select the text any more.
faq.pdfcompress.1.a: The way it shrinks a file is by redrawing each page as an image, so the text becomes picture. That is why it warns you in advance when the PDF contains real text. A scan was already an image so nothing is lost, but if the text has to survive, do not use this tool.
faq.pdfcompress.2.a: A PDF that was already compressed well can grow when redrawn. In that case it says it grew rather than claiming it shrank. Lowering the quality or resolution will shrink it, at the cost of sharpness.
faq.pdfcompress.3.q: How do I choose the resolution?
faq.pdfcompress.3.a: Low for documents that will only be read on screen, high for anything to be printed. Check the first-page preview to see the text is still legible, then decide.
faq.pdfcompress.4.a: No. The original page size is kept, so print sizes such as A4 stay intact.
faq.audiolevel.0.q: Why not just turn the volume up?
faq.audiolevel.0.a: That does not work — the loud parts clip first and the sound breaks. So the loud parts are pushed down to narrow the range (evening out) and only then is everything raised (boosting). The other order distorts.
faq.audiolevel.1.a: The gap between the loudest peak and the perceived loudness. A smaller number means the gap between the parts you could not hear and the parts that hurt has narrowed — it measures how even the loudness became.
faq.audiolevel.2.a: Speech usually takes strong settings well, but on music it also lifts breath and background noise until everything feels stuffy. Judge it with the waveform and your ears.
faq.audiolevel.3.q: Which formats can I save as?
faq.audiolevel.3.a: MP3 or WAV. The preview always plays lossless; the format is chosen when you download.
faq.audiolevel.4.q: Why is the target level not 0?
faq.audiolevel.4.a: Sitting exactly at 0 overflows on some playback devices and during conversion, which adds noise. Leaving a little headroom is safer.
faq.video2img.0.q: How is this different from a screenshot?
faq.video2img.0.a: A screenshot is tied to your screen resolution and catches the player’s UI as well. This pulls the original frame out of the video itself, so it comes at the source resolution with nothing extra.
faq.video2img.1.a: PNG is sharper for frames full of text or shapes. For live-action footage JPG is far smaller, and WebP smaller still.
faq.video2img.2.q: Where does the video get uploaded?
faq.video2img.2.a: Nowhere. Opening it and pulling frames out both finish inside your browser.
faq.video2img.3.q: It says there are too many frames.
faq.video2img.3.a: Widen the interval. It grabs at most 200 frames in one go — beyond that the browser struggles.
faq.videocompress.0.q: Why does it take as long as the video itself?
faq.videocompress.0.a: A browser has no way to re-assemble a video. Instead it plays it back and redraws it into a smaller frame as it goes, so a one-minute video takes about a minute. This is not a workaround but the only route available in a browser, which is why the remaining time is shown plainly.
faq.videocompress.1.q: Where does the video get uploaded?
faq.videocompress.1.a: Nowhere. The whole point is that footage with your face or your home in it never has to go to an unfamiliar site.
faq.videocompress.2.q: How much smaller does it get?
faq.videocompress.2.a: It depends on the original. Phone footage usually shrinks a lot; something already well compressed can grow instead. When that happens it says it grew rather than claiming it shrank.
faq.videocompress.3.q: Should I reduce the frame size or the quality first?
faq.videocompress.3.a: Frame size has the larger effect on file size. For something you will only watch on a phone, halving it still looks fine. For a big screen, leave the size and lower the quality.
faq.videocompress.4.q: Why is it saved as webm?
faq.videocompress.4.a: It picks the most widely supported of the formats a browser can capture. webm opens in current browsers and in most editing tools.
faq.pdf2text.0.q: Why not just drag-select and copy?
faq.pdf2text.0.a: A PDF stores only where each glyph sits, so dragging often breaks at every line or scrambles the order. This tool reads those coordinates, groups them into lines, and starts a new paragraph where the line spacing widens — bringing back something you can actually read.
faq.pdf2text.1.q: No text comes out at all.
faq.pdf2text.1.a: It is a scan of paper. That kind of PDF holds pictures, not text, so there is nothing to extract. This tool cannot read letters out of an image, and rather than handing back an empty result as if it succeeded, it tells you.
faq.pdf2text.2.q: Where does the document get uploaded?
faq.pdf2text.2.a: Nowhere. Opening and reading both finish inside your browser — which suits contracts and papers that must not leave.
faq.pdf2text.3.a: A table loses its cell positions and comes out as one run of text. If the table is the point, exporting the PDF to images is the better route.
faq.exifclean.0.q: Do photos really carry a location?
faq.exifclean.0.a: Phone cameras record the coordinates of where the shot was taken by default. That is how a single photo posted to a marketplace or social media can reveal where someone lives. This tool shows you what is in there first — “it has been removed” is hard to trust on its own.
faq.exifclean.1.a: No. The photo is not redrawn; only the metadata block inside the file is cut out. Not one byte of the image data changes. Redrawing through a canvas would strip the data but shave the quality once more.
faq.exifclean.2.q: Where does the photo get uploaded?
faq.exifclean.2.a: Nowhere. Uploading a photo to an unfamiliar server in order to remove its location data would defeat the purpose.
faq.exifclean.3.a: JPG only. PNG files rarely carry capture location.
faq.exifclean.4.q: Will the photo end up rotated?
faq.exifclean.4.a: The orientation flag is removed along with the rest, so some programs may show it turned. If that happens, rotate it in the image editor and save.
faq.filesplit.0.q: Why split instead of using cloud storage?
faq.filesplit.0.a: Company material and contracts often cannot go to the cloud at all. Split them and you can simply send several messages or emails. This tool never uploads the file anywhere.
faq.filesplit.1.q: Is the joined file really identical?
faq.filesplit.1.a: It is. Nothing is compressed or converted — the bytes are cut and put back as they were. A checksum is shown when splitting and again when joining, so matching values mean it is identical.
faq.filesplit.2.q: What if the pieces arrive out of order, or one is missing?
faq.filesplit.2.a: Each piece carries its number and the total in its name, so the order sorts itself out. If one is missing it tells you which before joining — join without knowing and you get a file that will not open.
faq.filesplit.3.q: Does the other person need this tool too?
faq.filesplit.3.a: Yes, they use the join side of this page. Nothing has to be installed.
faq.pdfsign.0.q: Do I still have to print, sign and scan?
faq.pdfsign.0.a: No. The signature you draw on screen is laid straight onto the page. No printer, no scanner.
faq.pdfsign.1.q: Where does the contract get uploaded?
faq.pdfsign.1.a: Nowhere. Opening it and laying on the signature both finish inside your browser. Uploading a contract to an unfamiliar server in order to sign it would defeat the purpose.
faq.pdfsign.2.q: Can I use a stamp image instead of a signature?
faq.pdfsign.2.a: Yes. Use “use an image file instead” for a seal or a signature you prepared earlier. A PNG with a transparent background comes out cleanest.
faq.pdfsign.3.a: This tool lays on a picture; it does not attach a digital signature certificate. If the other party requires a certificate-based e-signature, use a dedicated service. This suits ordinary “insert a signature image” needs.
faq.pdfsign.4.q: How do I sign several pages?
faq.pdfsign.4.a: Change the page, sign, and download once per page. You can also feed the downloaded file back in to carry on with the next page.
faq.text2pdf.0.q: Will non-Latin text come out broken?
faq.text2pdf.0.a: No. The built-in PDF fonts have no Hangul, kana or Han characters, which normally means embedding a font file. Here the letters are drawn using fonts the browser already has, so those scripts — and emoji — come out as they are.
faq.text2pdf.1.q: Can I select the text in the PDF it makes?
faq.text2pdf.1.a: No, because the letters are drawn as an image. In exchange the fonts never break anywhere. If the text has to stay selectable, exporting to PDF from a word processor is the right route.
faq.text2pdf.2.q: Where does my text get uploaded?
faq.text2pdf.2.a: Nowhere. A CV draft or something private never has to be pasted into an online converter.
faq.text2pdf.3.a: Yes. It breaks into pages to fit A4 automatically, and the page count is shown before you build it.
faq.text2pdf.4.q: My lines run off the right edge.
faq.text2pdf.4.a: They do not — wrapping happens character by character. Many scripts are written with few or no spaces, and wrapping only at word boundaries would push those lines off the page.
faq.qrread.0.q: Why does it tell me what is inside?
faq.qrread.0.a: A QR cannot be checked by eye. Scanning and opening it blindly is the same as clicking a link without reading the address. So a web address shows where it goes and a WiFi code shows which network, before anything else.
faq.qrread.1.q: Where does the image get uploaded?
faq.qrread.1.a: Nowhere. QR codes often carry invite links, WiFi passwords or account numbers, so uploading one to an unfamiliar site to read it is a bad trade.
faq.qrread.2.a: Yes. For a QR in front of you, read it with the camera. You have to allow camera access once.
faq.qrread.3.q: Sometimes it cannot read the code.
faq.qrread.3.a: A cropped or blurred code will not read. For a screenshot, crop again so the whole QR is inside.
faq.qr.0.q: Why are they in one place?
faq.qr.0.a: Wanting to check that the QR you just made actually scans is the natural next step. With the two apart, you would go looking for another site to do it.
faq.qr.1.a: The decoder used for reading is fetched only when you first open that tab. If the browser already has a reader built in, nothing is fetched at all.
faq.imgmerge.0.q: Screenshots of different widths come out ragged.
faq.imgmerge.0.a: Use “size matching” and the rest are adjusted to a reference width. Matching the largest keeps the quality; matching the smallest keeps the file small. Leftover space is filled with the background colour and each image is centred — aligning them left makes a staircase.
faq.imgmerge.1.q: Where do the photos get uploaded?
faq.imgmerge.1.a: Nowhere. Chat screenshots and receipts are exactly the sort of thing you would not want seen, so it all stays in the browser.
faq.imgmerge.2.q: How do I change the order?
faq.imgmerge.2.a: They join in the order you added them. To reorder, clear it and add them again in the order you want.
faq.imgmerge.3.q: It says the result is too large.
faq.imgmerge.3.a: There is a limit to the image size a browser can handle at once. Choose “match the smallest”, or split the photos into two batches.
faq.pdf.0.q: Where do the documents get uploaded?
faq.pdf.0.a: Nowhere. This is where contracts and CVs pass through, so it matters especially here. Opening and editing both finish inside your browser.
faq.pdf.1.a: The PDF engine is fetched only when you first open that tab. Features you never use do not slow anything down.
faq.pdf.2.a: Work on a PDF usually continues — merge, shrink, sign. Scattered apart, you would have to find a different place each time.
faq.sound.0.q: Why are they in one place?
faq.sound.0.a: Record → cut → level → join is usually one continuous job. Scattered apart, you would have to find a different place each time.
faq.sound.1.q: Which formats can I save as?
faq.sound.1.a: MP3 or WAV. MP3 is far smaller for sending or uploading; WAV is lossless and better if you will edit it again.
faq.sound.2.q: Where do the files get uploaded?
faq.sound.2.a: Nowhere. A meeting recording or a personal memo never leaves.
faq.favicon.0.q: Why do I need several sizes?
faq.favicon.0.a: Every place uses a different one. A browser tab shows 32px, the iPhone home screen 180px, Android 192 and 512px. Supply only one and it will end up mushy or missing somewhere.
faq.favicon.1.a: Older browsers and some tools still look for an .ico. An .ico is really a container for several sizes, so it is built holding 16, 32 and 48.
faq.favicon.2.q: Where does the image get uploaded?
faq.favicon.2.a: Nowhere. A logo you have not published yet never has to go to an unfamiliar site.
faq.favicon.3.q: What if my image is not square?
faq.favicon.3.a: It is centred and the leftover space is filled with the background. A square image still comes out cleanest — it tells you whether yours is square.
faq.favicon.4.q: Where do I put the code?
faq.favicon.4.a: Inside the HTML head. The same snippet is included as a text file in the ZIP.
faq.passgen.0.q: Where does the password I type go?
faq.passgen.0.a: Nowhere at all — no network request happens. Typing a password you really use into a “strength checker” site is risky; here there is nothing to worry about.
faq.passgen.1.q: Does it check whether the password has been breached?
faq.passgen.1.a: No. Doing that means sending part of the value to an outside service, and the moment it does, the promise that nothing is sent is broken. Instead it points out the weaknesses directly — common words, keyboard runs, years.
faq.passgen.2.q: How is the “time to crack” calculated?
faq.passgen.2.a: From the character sets used and the length it counts the possibilities, assuming modern hardware makes ten billion attempts a second. Any weakness found cuts it down — because in reality it would fall much faster.
faq.passgen.3.a: Length. Adding four characters beats sprinkling in a few symbols by a wide margin.
faq.passgen.4.a: l and I, O and 0 are hard to tell apart by eye. If you will ever write it down or read it aloud, leaving them out is safer.
faq.passgen.5.q: How safe is the “easy to remember” mode?
faq.passgen.5.a: Each piece has 1,900 possibilities, so five pieces give 1,900^5 × 100 ≈ 2^61 combinations. Even at ten billion attempts a second that averages about four years. For more, raise it to six or eight pieces.
faq.gradient.0.q: What is “keep the middle from going dead”?
faq.gradient.0.a: Blend two colours naively and the middle goes muddy — blue to yellow passing through grey is the classic case. Screen colour values are not proportional to perceived brightness; take that distortion out before blending and it does not happen. The comparison strip shows both side by side.
faq.gradient.1.q: When should I turn on “smooth it with more stops”?
faq.gradient.1.a: On a large background, where it makes the banding less visible. It works by inserting extra intermediate colours, so the CSS gets longer.
faq.gradient.2.q: Where do I paste the copied CSS?
faq.gradient.2.a: As that element’s background. The copied value already includes background:.
faq.tableconv.0.q: Can I paste straight from a spreadsheet?
faq.tableconv.0.a: Yes. Copying from a spreadsheet gives you tab-separated text, and that is recognised automatically. CSV and Markdown tables work too.
faq.tableconv.1.q: Why line up the Markdown pipes?
faq.tableconv.1.a: It looks identical when rendered. But people read the source — during a code review or a documentation edit, aligned columns are far easier to follow. Characters that occupy two cells, as CJK ones do, are counted as two.
faq.tableconv.2.q: What happens when I convert to JSON?
faq.tableconv.2.a: The first row becomes the field names and the remaining rows become a list of objects. If the first row is not a header, the names come out strange.
faq.tableconv.3.q: It says the column counts differ.
faq.tableconv.3.a: That usually means the paste was cut off. The result is built by filling the gaps with empty cells, but the content may be misaligned, so do check it.
faq.text2img.0.q: Does long text get cut off?
faq.text2img.0.a: No. The text size shrinks automatically until it all fits. Setting the size by hand can overflow, and when it does, it tells you.
faq.text2img.1.a: Wrapping happens character by character. Many scripts are written with few or no spaces, and wrapping only at word boundaries pushes lines off the right edge.
faq.text2img.2.a: It is blended to match the eye so the middle does not go dead. If you still dislike it, turn the gradient off and use a flat colour.
faq.text2img.3.a: Places where a picture reads better than text (Instagram, X), or notices whose formatting must not break.
faq.redact.0.q: Is it really erased, or just covered?
faq.redact.0.a: Erased. The pixels in the covered area are overwritten in place and the image is re-exported from that. Unlike drawing a rectangle on screen, prising the downloaded file apart finds nothing underneath.
faq.redact.1.q: Should I use pixelation or black-out?
faq.redact.1.a: Use black-out for anything that truly must be hidden. Pixelation is known to be reversible for text, and this tool says so when you pick it.
faq.redact.2.q: Does the photo’s location data come off too?
faq.redact.2.a: Yes. Because it is redrawn on export, the capture location and device details go with it. Even with nothing to hide, one pass through this tool strips that data.
faq.redact.3.q: Where does the image get uploaded?
faq.redact.3.a: Nowhere. It is handled inside your browser and never sent to a server.
faq.redact.4.a: “Undo the last one” takes back the most recent box, and “back to the start” restores the original image. Before you download, the original is still intact.
faq.pdfredact.0.q: How is this different from covering it with a black rectangle?
faq.pdfredact.0.a: A black rectangle is just a shape laid over the text — the text is still in the file. Copy and paste it out and everything appears. A great many document leaks by institutions happened exactly this way. This tool re-bakes the page as an image, so the text data itself is no longer in the file.
faq.pdfredact.1.q: I cannot select text in the PDF I got back.
faq.pdfredact.1.a: That is precisely why it is safe. Keeping the text would keep the redacted part too. If you need selectable text, this is not the right tool.
faq.pdfredact.2.q: Does text disappear from pages I did not redact?
faq.pdfredact.2.a: Yes. Every page is re-baked as an image, so the text data disappears from the whole document — including hidden notes and comments you could not see.
faq.pdfredact.3.q: Where does the file get uploaded?
faq.pdfredact.3.a: Nowhere. It is handled inside your browser and never sent to a server.
faq.pdfredact.4.a: Raise the sharpness. The sharper it is, the larger the file. For printing, the sharpest setting is the one to use.
faq.textredact.0.q: Will it erase numbers it should have left alone?
faq.textredact.0.a: Card numbers are checked with the Luhn formula, so a 16-digit order number survives. Korean resident registration numbers are checked for the gender digit and a valid date in the first six. If there is still a kind you want kept, switch that kind off.
faq.textredact.1.a: No. Automatic detection always misses something. This tool shows you a list of what it found, so read the result once before sending it.
faq.textredact.2.q: What if the same phone number appears several times?
faq.textredact.2.a: The same value gets the same number (Phone number 1, Phone number 2). That way the log still reads as a sequence after redaction.
faq.textredact.3.q: Where does the text get uploaded?
faq.textredact.3.a: Nowhere. It is handled inside your browser only — especially so, given the text contains personal data.
faq.textredact.4.q: What kinds does it look for?
