faq.textredact.4.a: Eight: Korean resident registration number, Korean mobile number, card number, email, bank account number, IP address, API key or token, and JWT.
faq.audiospeed.0.a: By default the pitch is left alone. The sound is cut into short pieces and the overlaps are melted together, adjusting only the spacing. Turn off “keep the voice” and the pitch shifts with the speed, the old-fashioned way.
faq.audiospeed.1.q: Can it slow things down as well?
faq.audiospeed.1.a: Yes, down to 0.5×. For transcription, or replaying a passage you could not catch, 0.75× is usually the useful one.
faq.audiospeed.2.a: The audio is extracted from the video and adjusted. The result comes out as an audio file.
faq.audiospeed.3.q: Where does the file get uploaded?
faq.audiospeed.3.a: Nowhere. It is handled inside your browser only.
faq.audiospeed.4.q: Does speeding it up hurt the quality?
faq.audiospeed.4.a: Pull it too far and the seams become audible. Speech takes up to 2× comfortably; music is better with only a small change.
faq.videorotate.0.a: At 90 and 270 degrees the output frame itself is flipped — a 320×180 video comes out 180×320. Leaving the frame as it was would squash or crop it.
faq.videorotate.1.a: Yes. The original audio is carried over as it is — only the picture is redrawn. Turn off “keep the sound” if you do not need it.
faq.videorotate.2.q: Can I do something else while it captures?
faq.videorotate.2.a: Keep this tab in front. Move to another tab and the browser stops drawing, leaving that stretch as a frozen frame. If that happens, you are told once it finishes.
faq.videorotate.3.q: What format does it come out as?
faq.videorotate.3.a: webm. Current devices and programs mostly play it as it is.
faq.videorotate.4.q: Where does the video get uploaded?
faq.videorotate.4.a: Nowhere. It is handled inside your browser only.
faq.pdfpagenum.0.q: Can I keep the number off the cover?
faq.pdfpagenum.0.a: Yes. Set how many leading pages to skip and no number goes on them. With “do not count skipped pages” on, the first page of the body becomes page 1.
faq.pdfpagenum.1.q: Can I write it as “page 3” in my own script?
faq.pdfpagenum.1.a: Yes. The number is drawn as an image of the text, so non-Latin scripts do not break. The built-in PDF fonts cannot hold them, which is why they usually do.
faq.pdfpagenum.2.q: Can the paper sizes be mixed?
faq.pdfpagenum.2.a: Yes. The margin is measured against each page’s size, so a mix of A4 and Letter does not make the number jump around.
faq.pdfpagenum.3.q: What happens to numbers that were already there?
faq.pdfpagenum.3.a: They are not removed; the new one goes on top. If the document already has numbers, place yours somewhere else.
faq.pdfpagenum.4.q: Where does the file get uploaded?
faq.pdfpagenum.4.a: Nowhere. It is handled inside your browser only.
faq.pdfcrop.0.q: Does cropping make the text unselectable?
faq.pdfcrop.0.a: No, it stays selectable. Pages are not baked into images — only the visible box is narrowed. The file size barely changes either.
faq.pdfcrop.1.a: No. It is only hidden, and another program can undo it later. To remove it for good, use the PDF redaction tool.
faq.pdfcrop.2.q: Pages ending up different sizes would be awkward.
faq.pdfcrop.2.a: “Same size for every page” is the default. One box that encloses every page is used, so nothing jumps as you page through.
faq.pdfcrop.3.q: The margins are not being cropped.
faq.pdfcrop.3.a: A single scan speck in a corner counts as content. Try raising “ignore faint specks”.
faq.pdfcrop.4.a: On a phone or an e-reader the text appears far larger in the same screen. It also saves paper when printing.
faq.imgresize.0.q: How do I hit a limit like “under 3MB”?
faq.imgresize.0.a: Choose “fit a size” and set the limit; it lowers the quality by itself until the file drops below it. If quality alone is not enough, it reduces the dimensions too. This is not something a person should be dragging a slider for.
faq.imgresize.1.q: Text goes mushy when I shrink a lot.
faq.imgresize.1.a: It steps down by halves rather than shrinking all at once. Even so, for an image full of text, staying with PNG or shrinking less is better.
faq.imgresize.2.q: Can shrinking make the file bigger?
faq.imgresize.2.a: “Never enlarge past the original” is the default, so the dimensions never grow. The file size can grow depending on the format, and when it does, that is what it says.
faq.imgresize.3.a: JPEG for photographs, WebP to go smaller still, PNG when there is a lot of text or diagrams.
faq.imgresize.4.q: Where does the photo get uploaded?
faq.imgresize.4.a: Nowhere. It is handled inside your browser only.
faq.imgresize.5.q: Can I shrink several at once?
faq.imgresize.5.a: This tool is for getting one image exactly right. For many at once, use batch image conversion — same settings for all, downloaded as a ZIP.
faq.audiofade.0.a: When a cut lands where the waveform is not at zero, the sound ends abruptly and the speaker turns that jump into a click. Easing the start and end down for a moment removes it.
faq.audiofade.1.q: Why not just use a long fade?
faq.audiofade.1.a: A three-second fade on a short clip smears it. This tool measures the amplitude at the edges and takes only as much as is needed.
faq.audiofade.2.q: Does the whole thing get quieter?
faq.audiofade.2.a: Only the edges are touched. The middle is untouched.
faq.audiofade.3.a: The audio is extracted from the video and processed. The result comes out as an audio file.
faq.audiofade.4.q: Where does the audio get uploaded?
faq.audiofade.4.a: Nowhere. It is handled inside your browser only.
faq.subtitle.0.q: The subtitles drift further out the longer it runs.
faq.subtitle.0.a: Shifting will not fix that. It comes from the video and the subtitles having different frame rates, so the times have to be stretched by a ratio. Look for entries like 23.976 ↔ 25 under “drifting further apart”.
faq.subtitle.1.q: My web player shows no subtitles.
faq.subtitle.1.a: Standard web players only take VTT. Hit “to VTT” to convert and download — the header and the time notation change together.
faq.subtitle.2.q: How do I know the shift was right?
faq.subtitle.2.a: The first and last cue times are shown side by side, before and after. Compare them with when those lines are spoken in the video.
faq.subtitle.3.q: What if I shift too far back?
faq.subtitle.3.a: Any cue that would land before 0 is pinned at 0, and you are told how many did.
faq.subtitle.4.q: Where do the subtitles get uploaded?
faq.subtitle.4.a: Nowhere. They are handled inside your browser only.
faq.icsmake.0.q: Will the time be wrong for someone in another country?
faq.icsmake.0.a: It will not. You enter the time in Korea time and the file records it in UTC. It shows you “Korea time ○○ = ○○ in the file”, so you can check before using it.
faq.icsmake.1.q: My calendar app will not take the file.
faq.icsmake.1.a: A comma or semicolon in the title breaks the format, and this tool handles that automatically. The line endings are written to spec as well.
faq.icsmake.2.q: The last day of an all-day event is missing.
faq.icsmake.2.a: This tool writes the end date one day later so that the final day is included. The .ics rules work that way, and it is the part people most often get wrong by hand.
faq.icsmake.3.q: How do I use it in an announcement?
faq.icsmake.3.a: Attach the downloaded file to your post. Anyone who opens it gets the event straight into their own calendar.
faq.icsmake.4.q: Where does the event get uploaded?
faq.icsmake.4.a: Nowhere. It is created inside your browser only.
faq.barcode.0.a: Code128 for anything mixing letters and digits, such as internal stock or sorting books. Retail product barcodes are EAN-13, which takes 13 digits and nothing else.
faq.barcode.1.q: What is the last digit of an EAN-13?
faq.barcode.1.a: The check digit. It is computed from the first 12, and entering only 12 fills it in for you. Enter 13 with a mismatching last digit and it tells you the right one.
faq.barcode.2.q: I printed it and the scanner will not read it.
faq.barcode.2.a: Do not trim the margins at the sides. A barcode finds its start from the white space to the left and right — this is the most common reason a home-made barcode fails. Keeping the bars at 2px or wider helps too.
faq.barcode.3.a: It cannot. A barcode holds Latin letters, digits and symbols only. When you need other scripts, use a QR code.
faq.barcode.4.q: Where does the value get uploaded?
faq.barcode.4.a: Nowhere. It is drawn inside your browser only.
faq.pdfdiff.0.q: How is this different from comparing the text?
faq.pdfdiff.0.a: A text comparison only catches changed sentences. A shifted table cell, or a missing seal or signature image, leaves the text identical and stays invisible. This tool also overlays the pages as images, so those changes get boxed as well.
faq.pdfdiff.1.a: Yes. A scan has no text layer so the sentence list stays empty, but the image comparison works as usual. Choosing “images only” is faster.
faq.pdfdiff.2.q: Do the files get uploaded to a server?
faq.pdfdiff.2.a: No. Reading and rendering the PDFs both happen inside your browser.
faq.pdfdiff.3.q: What if the page counts differ?
faq.pdfdiff.3.a: Pages present on only one side are marked “only in A” and “only in B”. If the paper sizes differ, they are overlaid against the larger one.
faq.ghosttype.0.a: No. The run lives inside the link, so there is no account and no server. Lose the link and the run is gone with it.
faq.ghosttype.1.a: It does not. The run is not stored on a server but carried in the address itself, so the same race opens for as long as the link exists.
faq.ghosttype.2.q: Can I race on my own text?
faq.ghosttype.2.a: Yes. Paste it into “use my own text” and it travels inside the link, so whoever opens it types the same thing. Up to 240 characters.
faq.ghosttype.3.a: The Korean way, by jamo. 값 needs ㄱ · ㅏ · ㅂ · ㅅ — four presses, so four keystrokes. Counting syllables would read lower than reality and disagree with figures measured elsewhere.
faq.duel.0.q: Do I need an account or an install?
faq.duel.0.a: Neither. Open the link and it starts.
faq.duel.1.q: Is the room stored on a server?
faq.duel.1.a: It is not. The public network is used only to introduce the two of you; everything after that travels directly between you.
faq.duel.2.q: I cannot connect to my opponent.
faq.duel.2.a: Company networks and some carriers block direct connections. Try again from a different network, such as mobile data.
faq.duel.3.a: Six, at random: guess the word from its initials, pick the larger number, pick the colour it is painted (not the one it spells), add two numbers, find the matching word, and reverse it. The time limit shortens as the rounds go on.
faq.timecapsule.0.q: How is this different from other date-locked services?
faq.timecapsule.0.a: Most keep the letter on a server and send it on the day. That means an administrator can read it early, and if the service shuts down the letter goes with it. Here the locked letter *is* the address, so there is nothing being held anywhere.
faq.timecapsule.1.q: Can I open it by changing my computer’s clock?
faq.timecapsule.1.a: No, because the key is not on your computer. A public randomness beacon only publishes that round’s value once the time arrives, and without that value the key cannot be assembled.
faq.timecapsule.2.q: What if I lose the address?
faq.timecapsule.2.a: The letter goes with it. No copy is kept on our side. For anything important, write the address down in more than one place.
faq.timecapsule.3.a: That public randomness beacon has to keep running for it to open. In exchange, no company can read the letter early.
faq.chain.0.q: Why run them in one go?
faq.chain.0.a: Calling the tools one at a time means a person or an AI copies the intermediate values across. A 64-character hash where one character goes wrong changes everything downstream — and it is invisible to the eye. Chaining them keeps the intermediate values from ever leaving.
faq.chain.1.q: Which tools can I put in?
faq.chain.1.a: Any tool whose core is separated out: hashes, Base64, VAT, business days, age, Korean keyboard fix, unit conversion and more. Give a name that does not exist and it tells you before running.
faq.chain.2.q: If something goes wrong, do I find out where?
faq.chain.2.a: Yes. Each step reports its own result, and on failure it says which step it stopped at. Showing only the final value would leave nothing to trace back through.
faq.chain.3.q: Does it work from an AI agent?
faq.chain.3.a: chain_run on the MCP server (karmolab-mcp) does the same job. It uses the same code as the screen, so the results cannot diverge.
faq.dailytype.0.a: One Hangul character is two to four jamo. Both 값 and 왔 take four presses. Counted the English way, the same person scores about half of their real Korean speed. So this counts the keystrokes Korea actually uses (by jamo).
faq.dailytype.1.a: Midnight in Korean time. It is fixed regardless of your device’s time zone, so wherever you open it, the same day gives the same sentences. With local time everyone would get different ones and the results could not be compared.
faq.dailytype.2.q: Where do the sentences come from?
faq.dailytype.2.a: They are taken from this site’s own tool descriptions. They are not hand-written samples, so they never go stale — and while typing you also learn what tools exist here.
faq.dailytype.3.q: Is it only once a day?
faq.dailytype.3.a: No. Today’s record is kept, but practice stays open. Blocking it would remove the reason to come back as well.
faq.dailycho.0.q: Why are the answers tool names?
faq.dailycho.0.a: Bundling a dictionary makes it heavy, and hand-written word lists go stale. These come from the tool aliases this site already has, so the puzzles grow as the tools do — and while guessing you learn what is here.
faq.dailycho.1.q: What if only one letter is wrong?
faq.dailycho.1.a: It shows as a yellow box. In a consonant quiz you often land on a different word with the same consonants, and painting all of those the same colour as a plain miss hides the fact that you are getting better.
faq.dailycho.2.a: Midnight in Korean time. It is fixed regardless of your device’s time zone, so wherever you open it the same day gives the same puzzle.
faq.dailycho.3.q: Does sharing the result leak the answers?
faq.dailycho.3.a: No. Only the coloured grid and how many you got. None of the answer letters go in.
faq.charconv.0.a: ＡＢ and AB only look different in width on screen, but to a computer they are different characters. That is why a pasted value finds 0 results, a login fails, or a spreadsheet lookup misses. It is the hardest kind of cause to spot by eye.
faq.charconv.1.q: The romanisation differs from the official rules?
faq.charconv.1.a: It applies the character mapping only, without sound changes. 신라 comes out as sinra while the official form is Silla. Doing it properly needs morpheme boundaries, which needs a dictionary. So rather than presenting a wrong value as right, it tells you where a sound would change.
faq.charconv.2.q: Why is there no simplified/traditional Chinese?
faq.charconv.2.a: That needs a table, not a rule. A hand-written table goes stale and leaks, so it goes in when a proper data source can be brought in.
faq.charconv.3.q: What is splitting into jamo good for?
faq.charconv.3.a: Building an initial-consonant search index, or looking at why text got mangled. What you split can be joined back too.
faq.comparepic.0.q: Do the photos go up to a server?
faq.comparepic.0.a: No. They are drawn in the browser and saved from here as well. You can cut the internet off.
faq.comparepic.1.q: What if the two are different sizes?
faq.comparepic.1.a: They are stacked to fit the larger one. Stretching the smaller one blurs it, but cropping to match would remove the very part you wanted to compare — which is exactly the case when you look at an upscale before and after.
faq.comparepic.2.q: Does it work on a phone?
faq.comparepic.2.a: Yes. You can drag with a finger, and with a keyboard the arrow keys move it too.
faq.comparepic.3.a: For showing how much changed — retouching before and after, an upscale before and after, a background removed and not.
faq.livecount.0.q: Why does “months” differ from other calculators?
faq.livecount.0.a: Months are counted by the calendar, not divided into 30-day chunks. One month after 31 January is 28 February, not 3 March. Dividing by 30 makes your age depend on which month you were born in.
faq.livecount.1.a: No. It simply multiplies your “times a day” by the days elapsed. Days you did none and days you did two are multiplied the same way, which is why the screen says it is a rough figure.
faq.livecount.2.q: What if I put in a future date?
faq.livecount.2.a: It counts the time remaining. It does not show a negative number.
faq.livecount.3.q: Does it keep running when I close the tab?
faq.livecount.3.a: No. The timer stops when you leave the screen. Otherwise a tool you closed would keep ticking once a second and eat your battery.
faq.mesh3d.0.q: Does the file go up to a server?
faq.mesh3d.0.a: No. Reading it and drawing it both finish inside the browser. It opens with the internet cut off.
faq.mesh3d.1.a: STL and OBJ carry numbers without a unit, so the numbers are shown without one. Software on the 3D-printing side usually reads them as mm.
faq.mesh3d.2.a: Not yet. STL and OBJ are simple formats that hold only the shape, so they can be read without a library; glTF and FBX also carry materials and animation and are a different thing altogether.
faq.mesh3d.3.q: The model does not show the colours in the file?
faq.mesh3d.3.a: STL has no colour at all, and an OBJ’s colours live in a separate file (.mtl). For now only the shape is drawn, in a single colour.
faq.charconv.4.q: What if one simplified character maps to several traditional ones?
faq.charconv.4.a: It converts to the first candidate and notes on screen which characters were ambiguous. 发 can be 發 (to send) or 髮 (hair) — only the meaning decides. Picking one silently would ship the wrong text.
faq.charconv.5.q: Does it convert by word as well?
faq.charconv.5.a: No — by character. Catching vocabulary differences such as 打印機 ↔ 打印机 needs a word dictionary, and that table is far larger.
